spawning.answer: Parrots appear in jungle, bamboo jungle and, in Bedrock, sparse jungle biomes.

drops.answer: In Bedrock, parrots drop 1–2 feathers when killed. Java’s Looting increase should not be applied to this Bedrock drop.

breeding.answer: Parrots cannot be bred, and do not have a normal baby variant.

taming.answer: Feed suitable seeds to a parrot, such as wheat, melon, pumpkin, beetroot or torchflower seeds. Cookies are poisonous and can kill it.

interactions.answer: Tamed parrots can sit on your shoulders, imitate nearby mob sounds and dance near a playing jukebox. Never feed them cookies.

identity.answer: A parrot is a tameable jungle bird. Tame it with suitable seeds, let it perch on your shoulder, and listen to its imitations of nearby mobs. Cookies are poisonous to parrots.

behavior.answer: A parrot is a tameable jungle bird. Tame it with suitable seeds, let it perch on your shoulder, and listen to its imitations of nearby mobs. Cookies are poisonous to parrots.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Tame it with suitable seeds, let it perch on your shoulder, and listen to its imitations of nearby mobs. Cookies are poisonous to parrots.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 6 health points (3 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

spawning.answer: Phantoms appear around players who have gone several in-game days without resting. Bedrock spawning also depends on local darkness and monster-spawning rules; resting resets the relevant timer.

drops.answer: A player-killed phantom can drop 0–1 phantom membranes, with Looting increasing applicable amounts.

combat.answer: Phantoms swoop down from the sky and burn in daylight. Shelter can stop their attacks, and cats repel them.

interactions.answer: Entering a bed resets the rest timer associated with phantom spawning. The doInsomnia game rule also affects whether they can spawn in Bedrock.

taming.answer: Phantom cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Phantom cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A phantom is a flying hostile mob associated with players going too long without rest. Sleep or rest to avoid attracting more phantoms, and watch for diving attacks at night.

behavior.answer: A phantom is a flying hostile mob associated with players going too long without rest. Sleep or rest to avoid attracting more phantoms, and watch for diving attacks at night.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Pigs appear on grass in many Overworld biomes and some village animal pens. Natural climate variants depend on their spawning biome.

drops.answer: Adult pigs can drop raw porkchops, or cooked porkchops when killed while burning. An equipped saddle also drops; babies do not have normal adult loot.

breeding.answer: Feed carrots, potatoes or beetroot to two adult pigs. The baby inherits one parent’s variant.

taming.answer: Pigs are not tamed like wolves. Food attracts them, and a saddle allows riding rather than ownership.

transport.answer: Equip a pig with a saddle and hold a carrot on a stick to steer it.

interactions.answer: Lightning can transform a pig into a zombified piglin. A saddle is equipment, not a breeding or taming item.

identity.answer: A pig is a passive farm animal. Raise it for porkchops or ride a saddled pig using a carrot on a stick to steer.

behavior.answer: A pig is a passive farm animal. Raise it for porkchops or ride a saddled pig using a carrot on a stick to steer.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Raise it for porkchops or ride a saddled pig using a carrot on a stick to steer.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

spawning.answer: Piglins appear in Nether wastes, crimson forests and bastion remnants. They do not naturally populate every Nether biome.

drops.answer: Piglin loot depends on equipment and what it was carrying. A charged-creeper kill can produce a piglin head. Bartering returns are a separate mechanic, not ordinary death loot.

trading.answer: Give an adult piglin a gold ingot to barter. Gold nuggets and other gold items are not substitutes for the ingot. Babies do not perform normal adult bartering, and piglin brutes do not barter.

combat.answer: Wearing a piece of gold armor can prevent ordinary piglin hostility, but attacking piglins or disturbing protected containers or gold blocks can still anger them. Gold armor does not pacify piglin brutes.

interactions.answer: Outside the Nether, piglins can become zombified piglins. Adult bartering and baby item-pickup behavior are different.

taming.answer: Piglin cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Piglin cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A piglin is a Nether mob that can barter gold ingots for items. Wearing gold armor helps avoid ordinary piglin hostility, but certain actions still anger it. Piglin brutes do not follow the same rules.

behavior.answer: A piglin is a Nether mob that can barter gold ingots for items. Wearing gold armor helps avoid ordinary piglin hostility, but certain actions still anger it. Piglin brutes do not follow the same rules.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 16 health points (8 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Piglin brutes generate in bastion remnants. They do not naturally respawn after being killed.

drops.answer: Piglin brutes have a chance to drop their golden axe under suitable kill conditions, and give experience. They do not provide ordinary piglin barter loot.

trading.answer: Piglin brutes do not barter and are not distracted or pacified by gold ingots.

combat.answer: Piglin brutes are always hostile to players and are not pacified by gold armor. They have much more health than ordinary piglins.

taming.answer: Piglin brute cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Piglin brute cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A piglin brute is an aggressive axe-wielding mob found in bastion remnants. It does not become friendly because you wear gold and does not barter like ordinary piglins.

behavior.answer: A piglin brute is an aggressive axe-wielding mob found in bastion remnants. It does not become friendly because you wear gold and does not barter like ordinary piglins.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 50 health points (25 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Pillagers appear at pillager outposts, in patrols and during raids. Outpost spawning and patrol spawning are separate systems.

drops.answer: In Bedrock, pillagers can drop arrows and have a separate chance to drop their crossbow. Raid loot can include other items, and an eligible captain can drop an ominous bottle and banner.

combat.answer: Pillagers use crossbows and attack from range. Shielding, solid cover and separating a group can help. Do not assume Java-only disarmed-pillager tricks work in Bedrock.

interactions.answer: An ominous bottle can start the Bad Omen and Raid Omen sequence when used under the relevant conditions; killing a captain is not the same as directly starting every raid.

taming.answer: Pillager cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Pillager cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A pillager is a hostile illager armed with a crossbow. It attacks from range and appears in patrols, outposts, and raids.

behavior.answer: A pillager is a hostile illager armed with a crossbow. It attacks from range and appears in patrols, outposts, and raids.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 24 health points (12 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Players enter at the world spawn or a valid personal respawn location. Beds and respawn anchors have dimension-specific rules.

drops.answer: With keepInventory off, a dying Survival player normally drops carried inventory and some experience. Creative mode and world rules change the outcome.

health.answer: A player normally has 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects and game settings can change survivability.

identity.answer: A player is a person-controlled character in the world. Players explore, build, craft, fight, and interact with the world according to their game mode and permissions.

behavior.answer: A player is a person-controlled character in the world. Players explore, build, craft, fight, and interact with the world according to their game mode and permissions.

spawning.answer: Look in snowy plains, ice spikes, frozen oceans and deep frozen oceans. Bedrock also has polar-bear spawning in some frozen rivers and snowy mountain biomes.

drops.answer: Polar bears can drop cod and salmon under their loot conditions. They do not drop fur or a hide item.

breeding.answer: Polar bears cannot be bred by players.

taming.answer: Polar bears cannot be tamed. Feeding them fish does not make them pets.

combat.answer: Adults can become hostile when a cub is nearby or when attacked. Give groups with cubs plenty of room.

identity.answer: A polar bear is a large animal found in cold regions. Adults may become hostile when provoked or when a cub is threatened; it is not a tameable riding animal.

behavior.answer: A polar bear is a large animal found in cold regions. Adults may become hostile when provoked or when a cub is threatened; it is not a tameable riding animal.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 30 health points (15 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: In Bedrock, look for pufferfish in warm oceans near suitable surface spawning water; do not apply Java’s wider ocean-biome list.

drops.answer: Pufferfish drop the pufferfish item and can also drop bones in Bedrock. Java’s bone-meal drop is a different edition rule.

breeding.answer: Pufferfish cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Pufferfish cannot be tamed. Use a water bucket to capture one.

combat.answer: Pufferfish inflate near threats and can poison nearby players. The item is also poisonous to eat; do not confuse safely collecting one with safely eating it.

identity.answer: A pufferfish is an aquatic fish that inflates when threatened. Its defenses can poison nearby entities. Collect it in a bucket or use its item form in compatible brewing recipes.

behavior.answer: A pufferfish is an aquatic fish that inflates when threatened. Its defenses can poison nearby entities. Collect it in a bucket or use its item form in compatible brewing recipes.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 3 health points (1.5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Rabbits appear in deserts, meadows, flower forests, taigas and several snowy biomes. Their natural fur colors depend on the biome; gold rabbits are associated with deserts and white variants with snowy areas.

drops.answer: Adult rabbits can drop rabbit hide and raw rabbit, or cooked rabbit when killed while burning. A rabbit’s foot is a separate rare player-kill drop.

breeding.answer: Feed carrots, golden carrots or dandelions to two adult rabbits. Babies usually inherit a parent’s fur, with a small chance to match the local biome.

taming.answer: Rabbits cannot be tamed as owned pets. Suitable food attracts them and can be used for breeding.

variants.answer: Normal rabbits have several biome-linked fur colors. The hostile killer bunny is a Java-only feature, not an ordinary Bedrock rabbit variant.

combat.answer: Ordinary Bedrock rabbits are passive toward players. The hostile killer bunny is a Java-only feature, not an ordinary Bedrock rabbit variant.

identity.answer: A rabbit is a small passive animal. Breed it with suitable food and raise rabbits for hide, meat, and occasional rabbit's feet.

behavior.answer: A rabbit is a small passive animal. Breed it with suitable food and raise rabbits for hide, meat, and occasional rabbit's feet.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 3 health points (1.5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

spawning.answer: Ravagers appear as part of raids, sometimes with an illager rider. They are not ordinary naturally spawning plains animals.

drops.answer: In Bedrock, a player-killed ravager drops a saddle. Its rider has separate loot; killing the mount does not mean every rider has died.

combat.answer: Ravagers have powerful melee attacks and a roar. A shield can help against their attack, but stay alert for the follow-up roar and any rider.

taming.answer: Ravagers cannot be tamed or ridden by a player in normal Survival.

breeding.answer: Ravager cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A ravager is a large hostile beast found in raids. It attacks with powerful close-range strikes and can damage certain plants, so keep your distance and use cover.

behavior.answer: A ravager is a large hostile beast found in raids. It attacks with powerful close-range strikes and can damage certain plants, so keep your distance and use cover.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 100 health points (50 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Salmon swim in rivers and frozen rivers, plus several ocean types. Bedrock includes ordinary and lukewarm ocean variants as well as cold and frozen oceans.

drops.answer: Salmon drop raw salmon, or cooked salmon when killed while burning. In Bedrock they can also drop bones, with the bone amount affected by the fish’s size and applicable loot conditions.

breeding.answer: Salmon cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Salmon cannot be tamed. Capture one with a water bucket to transport it.

variants.answer: Salmon have small, medium and large sizes. Their size is separate from their raw-salmon item drop.

identity.answer: A salmon is an aquatic fish found in suitable water areas. Catch it for food or collect it alive in a water bucket.

behavior.answer: A salmon is an aquatic fish found in suitable water areas. Catch it for food or collect it alive in a water bucket.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Catch it for food or collect it alive in a water bucket.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 3 health points (1.5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Sheep appear on suitable grass in many Overworld biomes and some villages. Their natural wool-color distribution depends on the climate of the spawning biome.

drops.answer: Adult sheep can drop mutton and, if not already sheared, wool matching their color. Burning changes mutton to cooked mutton. Shearing a living adult gives wool without killing it.

breeding.answer: Feed wheat to two adult sheep. Compatible parental wool colors can mix in the baby; otherwise it inherits a parent’s color.

interactions.answer: Use shears to harvest wool and dye to change its color. Sheep regrow wool by eating grass. The jeb_ name effect changes appearance, not the underlying harvested wool color.

taming.answer: Sheep cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

identity.answer: A sheep is a passive farm animal that provides wool. Use shears to collect wool, dye it to change wool color, and feed adult sheep wheat to breed them.

behavior.answer: A sheep is a passive farm animal that provides wool. Use shears to collect wool, dye it to change wool color, and feed adult sheep wheat to breed them.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Use shears to collect wool, dye it to change wool color, and feed adult sheep wheat to breed them.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 8 health points (4 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

spawning.answer: Shulkers generate in End cities on the outer End islands. Their reproduction involves shulker-bullet interactions, not food-based animal breeding.

drops.answer: In Bedrock, shulkers can drop shulker shells with a quantity-based Looting increase. Do not substitute Java’s shell drop-chance formula.

breeding.answer: Shulkers do not breed with food. They can duplicate through suitable shulker-bullet interactions, including a special Bedrock behavior when a shulker bullet kills one.

combat.answer: Their homing bullets inflict Levitation, making the eventual fall dangerous. A closed shell provides protection, and shulkers can teleport away when hurt.

interactions.answer: Shulkers can be dyed in Bedrock. Their shell color is separate from the shell item they drop.

taming.answer: Shulker cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

identity.answer: A shulker is a hostile shell-covered mob found in End cities. Its projectiles cause Levitation, and its shells are used to craft portable shulker boxes.

behavior.answer: A shulker is a hostile shell-covered mob found in End cities. Its projectiles cause Levitation, and its shells are used to craft portable shulker boxes.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 30 health points (15 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Shulkers fire homing bullets at targets.

combat.answer: A shulker bullet can cause Levitation. Destroy or avoid it and prepare for the fall if hit. These are not collectible ammunition items.

identity.answer: A shulker bullet is a homing projectile fired by a shulker. A hit can cause Levitation; destroy it or use cover to avoid being lifted into a dangerous fall.

behavior.answer: A shulker bullet is a homing projectile fired by a shulker. A hit can cause Levitation; destroy it or use cover to avoid being lifted into a dangerous fall.

spawning.answer: Silverfish emerge from infested blocks and from the spawner in a stronghold’s End portal room. Other sources include suitable trial spawners and the Infested effect.

drops.answer: Silverfish have no normal item drops; a player or tamed-wolf kill gives experience.

combat.answer: Damaging one can wake nearby silverfish hidden in infested blocks. Avoid carelessly mining through an infested cluster during a fight.

interactions.answer: Breaking an infested block normally releases a silverfish, but Silk Touch can prevent that release. Silverfish and endermites are different mobs.

taming.answer: Silverfish cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Silverfish cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A silverfish is a small hostile mob associated with infested stone and strongholds. Disturbing infested blocks can release it, and nearby infested blocks can make a fight worse.

behavior.answer: A silverfish is a small hostile mob associated with infested stone and strongholds. Disturbing infested blocks can release it, and nearby infested blocks can make a fight worse.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 8 health points (4 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Skeletons appear in suitable dark Overworld locations and from certain monster or trial spawners. Nether sources include soul sand valleys and Nether fortresses.

drops.answer: Skeletons can drop bones and arrows, with separate chances for naturally equipped gear. Picked-up equipment has different rules. A charged-creeper kill can produce a skeleton skull.

combat.answer: Skeletons fire arrows and generally burn in daylight unless protected. Use a shield or solid cover and close the distance carefully.

interactions.answer: Keeping an ordinary skeleton in powder snow can convert it into a stray. That does not mean every skeleton-like mob converts the same way.

taming.answer: Skeleton cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Skeleton cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A skeleton is a hostile undead mob that usually fires arrows. Use cover or a shield against it. Ordinary exposed skeletons burn in sunlight unless protected.

behavior.answer: A skeleton is a hostile undead mob that usually fires arrows. Use cover or a shield against it. Ordinary exposed skeletons burn in sunlight unless protected.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Skeleton horses can appear as skeleton traps associated with natural thunderstorms. Approaching a trap can produce several mounted skeleton horsemen; Channeling lightning does not create that natural trap.

drops.answer: A skeleton horse can drop bones under the applicable death conditions. In Bedrock, an untriggered trap horse has no item or experience drops. The skeleton rider has its own separate loot.

taming.answer: In Bedrock, skeleton horses are already tamed. You do not tame them by repeatedly feeding or riding them like an ordinary horse.

breeding.answer: Skeleton horses cannot be bred.

transport.answer: In Bedrock, skeleton horses can be ridden and controlled without a saddle. Java’s saddle requirement is not the Bedrock rule.

combat.answer: The skeleton horse itself is passive. A skeleton horseman is dangerous because of its separate skeleton rider; killing the rider can leave the horse alive.

identity.answer: A skeleton horse is an undead rideable horse. Certain skeleton-trap encounters can produce them. It is not an ordinary breedable horse.

behavior.answer: A skeleton horse is an undead rideable horse. Certain skeleton-trap encounters can produce them. It is not an ordinary breedable horse.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 15 health points (7.5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Look for slimes in swamps or mangrove swamps between Y=51 and Y=69 in dim light; full moons are better and new moons do not produce swamp slimes. They also spawn below Y=40 in special slime chunks regardless of light. In Bedrock, slime-chunk positions are the same across world seeds. Suitable trial spawners and the Oozing effect are other sources.

drops.answer: The smallest slimes can drop slimeballs. Larger slimes split into smaller ones, so finish the smaller sizes to collect their slimeball drops. The total yield depends on how many children appear and the loot conditions.

health.answer: Normal large slimes have 16 health points, medium slimes have 4 and small slimes have 1. Special sizes can have different values.

combat.answer: Larger slimes hurt you by contact and split when killed. Small slimes do not deal normal contact damage, but can still push or distract you.

taming.answer: Slime cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Slime cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults. Larger ones split into smaller ones when killed; that is not food-based breeding.

identity.answer: A slime is a bouncing hostile mob that divides into smaller slimes when killed. Its smaller forms can provide slimeballs used for sticky pistons and other recipes.

behavior.answer: A slime is a bouncing hostile mob that divides into smaller slimes when killed. Its smaller forms can provide slimeballs used for sticky pistons and other recipes.

spawning.answer: Blazes shoot small fireballs, and dispensers launch them from fire charges.

combat.answer: Small fireballs can ignite targets and blocks. They are not the same explosive, deflectable projectile as a ghast fireball.

identity.answer: A small fireball is a fiery projectile used by mobs such as blazes. It can burn targets and ignite suitable surfaces, so use cover rather than trying to collect it.

behavior.answer: A small fireball is a fiery projectile used by mobs such as blazes. It can burn targets and ignite suitable surfaces, so use cover rather than trying to collect it.

spawning.answer: Sniffers hatch from sniffer eggs. Search suspicious sand in warm ocean ruins for eggs, or obtain an egg by breeding two sniffers; they do not simply spawn across ordinary terrain.

drops.answer: Sniffers have no normal item drops on death. Torchflower seeds and pitcher pods are dug up by living adults; sniffer eggs come from breeding.

breeding.answer: In Bedrock, bring two adult sniffers to full health and feed them torchflower seeds. They produce a sniffer egg rather than a live baby. A placed egg hatches faster on a moss block.

interactions.answer: Adult sniffers dig torchflower seeds and pitcher pods from suitable ground after a cooldown. They cannot dig every block; mycelium does not work.

taming.answer: Sniffer cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

identity.answer: A sniffer is an ancient passive animal hatched from a sniffer egg. It digs up special ancient plant seeds or pods from suitable ground, helping players grow decorative plants.

behavior.answer: A sniffer is an ancient passive animal hatched from a sniffer egg. It digs up special ancient plant seeds or pods from suitable ground, helping players grow decorative plants.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. It digs up special ancient plant seeds or pods from suitable ground, helping players grow decorative plants.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 14 health points (7 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

spawning.answer: Snow golems are constructed rather than naturally spawning as ordinary wildlife.

construction.answer: Stack two snow blocks and place a carved pumpkin or jack o’lantern on top last. Leave enough room for the resulting snow golem.

drops.answer: Snow golems can drop snowballs on death. Shearing a living golem removes its carved pumpkin; that is a separate interaction.

combat.answer: Snow golems throw snowballs at hostile targets, but most mobs do not take direct damage from ordinary snowballs. Blazes are an important exception.

interactions.answer: Snow golems can leave a snow trail where the environment allows it. Rain, water and hot surroundings can harm them. Shears remove the pumpkin head.

taming.answer: Snow golem cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Snow golem cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults. They are created using their construction or summoning method instead.

identity.answer: A snow golem is a player-built mob made using snow blocks and a carved pumpkin or suitable equivalent. It throws snowballs at many hostile mobs and can leave snow trails in suitable conditions. Heat and water can harm it.

behavior.answer: A snow golem is a player-built mob made using snow blocks and a carved pumpkin or suitable equivalent. It throws snowballs at many hostile mobs and can leave snow trails in suitable conditions. Heat and water can harm it.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 4 health points (2 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Throw a snowball or fire one from a dispenser. Snow golems also throw snowballs.

combat.answer: Snowballs push or provoke many targets without normal weapon damage, but they can damage blazes. They are not a substitute for a weapon against every hostile mob.

identity.answer: A snowball is a throwable item and projectile. Throw it to knock or distract suitable targets; it also has special interactions with some mobs, including blazes.

behavior.answer: A snowball is a throwable item and projectile. Throw it to knock or distract suitable targets; it also has special interactions with some mobs, including blazes.

spawning.answer: Spiders appear in suitable dark Overworld locations, and from certain monster or trial spawners. They need more horizontal room than many humanoid mobs.

drops.answer: Spiders can drop string, and a player kill can also produce a spider eye. Looting affects the applicable drops.

combat.answer: Spiders climb walls and can become hostile in darkness or after being attacked. Bright light affects their normal aggression. Cave spiders are smaller and have different poison behavior.

taming.answer: Spider cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Spider cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A spider is a climbing mob that can become hostile depending on conditions. It climbs walls and attacks at close range. Brightness affects its ordinary aggression.

behavior.answer: A spider is a climbing mob that can become hostile depending on conditions. It climbs walls and attacks at close range. Brightness affects its ordinary aggression.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 16 health points (8 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Throw a splash potion or launch it with a dispenser to create the projectile.

interactions.answer: A splash potion breaks on impact and applies its effect nearby. The effect depends on the potion, and distance can affect its strength or duration.

identity.answer: A splash potion is a throwable potion. Throw it to apply its effect around the impact point; the effect depends on the potion's contents.

behavior.answer: A splash potion is a throwable potion. Throw it to apply its effect around the impact point; the effect depends on the potion's contents.

spawning.answer: Squid appear in suitable surface waters in oceans and rivers. Bedrock surface-spawn rules differ from the underground spawning of glow squid.

drops.answer: Squid can drop 1–3 ink sacs, with Looting increasing applicable amounts. Ordinary squid do not drop glow ink sacs.

breeding.answer: Squid cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Squid cannot be tamed.

identity.answer: A squid is a passive aquatic animal. It provides ink sacs when killed; it is not a tameable riding animal.

behavior.answer: A squid is a passive aquatic animal. It provides ink sacs when killed; it is not a tameable riding animal.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. It provides ink sacs when killed; it is not a tameable riding animal.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 10 health points (5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Strays replace some skeleton spawns in snowy biomes. Bedrock includes frozen rivers, frozen oceans and certain snowy mountain biomes. Ordinary skeletons can also become strays after remaining in powder snow.

drops.answer: Strays can drop bones, arrows and, under suitable player-kill conditions, an arrow of Slowness. Carried equipment has separate rules.

combat.answer: Strays shoot arrows that inflict Slowness. They are undead ranged attackers, so cover and a shield are useful.

interactions.answer: Powder snow can convert an ordinary skeleton into a stray. Bogged and parched do not use that same conversion rule.

taming.answer: Stray cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Stray cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A stray is a cold-region skeleton variant. It fires arrows that inflict Slowness, making it harder to escape follow-up attacks.

behavior.answer: A stray is a cold-region skeleton variant. It fires arrows that inflict Slowness, making it harder to escape follow-up attacks.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Striders naturally appear on lava in every Nether biome where their spawning conditions are met.

drops.answer: Adult striders drop 2–5 string and any equipped saddle. In Bedrock, their string drop is not increased by Looting.

breeding.answer: Feed warped fungus to two adult striders.

taming.answer: Striders do not require taming. Equip a saddle to ride one, then use a warped fungus on a stick to steer.

transport.answer: Ride a saddled strider across lava using a warped fungus on a stick. It slows down when cold and out of lava; water is dangerous to it.

identity.answer: A strider is a passive Nether animal that walks on lava. Saddle it and steer with a warped fungus on a stick for lava travel. It becomes cold and slower away from lava.

behavior.answer: A strider is a passive Nether animal that walks on lava. Saddle it and steer with a warped fungus on a stick for lava travel. It becomes cold and slower away from lava.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Saddle it and steer with a warped fungus on a stick for lava travel. It becomes cold and slower away from lava.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 20 health points (10 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

spawning.answer: Sulfur cubes appear in sulfur caves in game versions that include that feature. Large cubes can split into small cubes.

health.answer: Large sulfur cubes have 8 health points and small sulfur cubes have 4.

drops.answer: A large sulfur cube drops the block it absorbed when it dies. Small cubes do not provide the same experience drop.

interactions.answer: Sulfur cubes can absorb supported blocks, changing their properties. Use shears to remove an absorbed block. A dangerous absorbed block, such as TNT or magma, can make an otherwise passive cube hazardous.

taming.answer: Sulfur cube cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Sulfur cubes do not breed by pairing adults with food. When a large sulfur cube dies without exploding, it splits into two small cubes; those can grow into large ones.

identity.answer: A sulfur cube is a cube-shaped animal that can carry a suitable block. The block it holds can change its movement and other behavior. Some interactions can make it dangerous, including explosive behavior.

behavior.answer: A sulfur cube is a cube-shaped animal that can carry a suitable block. The block it holds can change its movement and other behavior. Some interactions can make it dangerous, including explosive behavior.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. The block it holds can change its movement and other behavior. Some interactions can make it dangerous, including explosive behavior.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

spawning.answer: Tadpoles hatch from frogspawn laid by breeding frogs. They are the growing stage that becomes a frog.

drops.answer: Tadpoles do not drop items or experience when killed.

breeding.answer: Tadpoles cannot breed; grow them into adult frogs first, then breed the frogs with slimeballs.

interactions.answer: Use a water bucket to move a tadpole and slimeballs to accelerate its growth. The biome where it matures determines the frog variant; its parents’ colors do not force the result.

taming.answer: Tadpole cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

identity.answer: A tadpole is the young aquatic stage of a frog. Carry it in a water bucket and raise it into a frog. Its growing environment affects which frog variant it becomes.

behavior.answer: A tadpole is the young aquatic stage of a frog. Carry it in a water bucket and raise it into a frog. Its growing environment affects which frog variant it becomes.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Carry it in a water bucket and raise it into a frog. Its growing environment affects which frog variant it becomes.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 6 health points (3 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

spawning.answer: Throw a trident to create its projectile; some drowned also throw tridents.

interactions.answer: A player’s thrown trident can be recovered, and Loyalty can return it. Channeling and Riptide have their own weather or water requirements. A drowned’s thrown projectile is not a freely recoverable player trident.

identity.answer: A thrown trident is a trident travelling as a projectile. It deals damage on impact; recovery and return behavior depend on the trident and its enchantments.

behavior.answer: A thrown trident is a trident travelling as a projectile. It deals damage on impact; recovery and return behavior depend on the trident and its enchantments.

spawning.answer: Igniting TNT creates the primed TNT entity. Redstone, fire and other explosion-related triggers can ignite it.

interactions.answer: Primed TNT counts down and explodes, damaging nearby entities and breaking blocks. Water can protect blocks from much explosion damage without making nearby entities safe.

identity.answer: TNT is an explosive block that becomes a primed explosive entity when ignited. Use it for controlled explosions, keeping people, pets, and important builds well away from the blast.

behavior.answer: TNT is an explosive block that becomes a primed explosive entity when ignited. Use it for controlled explosions, keeping people, pets, and important builds well away from the blast.

spawning.answer: Place a crafted TNT minecart on rails.

interactions.answer: A powered activator rail can prime a TNT minecart. Other violent impacts or damage conditions can also trigger it, so keep it away from valuable builds.

drops.answer: Breaking an unprimed TNT minecart normally returns its item. An exploding TNT minecart is not a safe way to recover the cart.

identity.answer: A TNT minecart is an explosive rail vehicle. Certain activations and impacts can trigger it. Use it only where an explosion is intended.

behavior.answer: A TNT minecart is an explosive rail vehicle. Certain activations and impacts can trigger it. Use it only where an explosion is intended.

spawning.answer: Trader llamas arrive with wandering traders. They can also be produced by breeding suitable tamed trader llamas.

taming.answer: A trader llama still leashed to its wandering trader cannot be ridden normally. In Bedrock, detaching it from that trader makes it tamed and prevents normal trader-llama despawning.

breeding.answer: Feed hay bales to two tamed adult trader llamas. Their baby retains the trader-llama type and special rug.

transport.answer: Trader llamas can carry storage and form caravans. A rug is not a steering saddle; they are not controlled like horses.

drops.answer: Adult trader llamas can drop leather plus their applicable equipment and stored contents. Their lead is a separate item when detached.

health.answer: Trader llamas have a maximum health between 15 and 30 health points. Different individual llamas can have different maximum health.

identity.answer: A trader llama is a llama associated with a wandering trader. It carries the trader's decorations and can defend itself by spitting. It follows llama-style handling rules rather than villager trading rules.

behavior.answer: A trader llama is a llama associated with a wandering trader. It carries the trader's decorations and can defend itself by spitting. It follows llama-style handling rules rather than villager trading rules.

combat.answer: It can attack under particular conditions, so do not assume it is always harmless. It carries the trader's decorations and can defend itself by spitting. It follows llama-style handling rules rather than villager trading rules.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

spawning.answer: The tripod camera is an Education feature, not a naturally spawning Survival creature. It is not normally obtainable in standard Bedrock Survival.

interactions.answer: In Minecraft Education, cameras work with portfolios to collect photos. This tripod entity is different from the camera command used by world creators.

identity.answer: A tripod camera is a special camera entity used in compatible Education features. It is not a normal Survival mob or a general-purpose companion.

behavior.answer: A tripod camera is a special camera entity used in compatible Education features. It is not a normal Survival mob or a general-purpose companion.

spawning.answer: In Bedrock, tropical fish appear in warm and lukewarm ocean variants, suitable lush-cave waters and applicable mangrove-swamp waters. They have many combinations of pattern and color.

drops.answer: Tropical fish drop the tropical-fish item and can also drop bones in Bedrock. A living bucket of tropical fish is obtained by capturing one, not by killing it.

breeding.answer: Tropical fish cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Tropical fish cannot be tamed. Capture one with a water bucket to preserve a living fish and its appearance.

variants.answer: Tropical fish have many color and pattern combinations. A bucket can preserve the captured fish’s appearance; the loose tropical-fish food item does not represent a living patterned fish.

identity.answer: A tropical fish is a colorful aquatic fish with many appearance variants. Collect it alive in a water bucket for aquariums or use a bucket of tropical fish for compatible axolotl interactions.

behavior.answer: A tropical fish is a colorful aquatic fish with many appearance variants. Collect it alive in a water bucket for aquariums or use a bucket of tropical fish for compatible axolotl interactions.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Collect it alive in a water bucket for aquariums or use a bucket of tropical fish for compatible axolotl interactions.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 3 health points (1.5 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

spawning.answer: Turtles naturally appear on sandy beaches, not snowy beaches or stony shores. In Bedrock their natural beach spawning is around Y=60–67. Turtle eggs are another source.

drops.answer: Adult turtles can drop seagrass. A lightning kill has a separate bowl-drop rule. Turtle scutes are produced when babies grow into adults, not by killing adults.

breeding.answer: Feed seagrass to two adult turtles. The pregnant turtle returns to its home beach to lay eggs on suitable sand; protect the eggs from trampling and hostile mobs.

interactions.answer: A baby turtle drops a scute when it becomes an adult. Move eggs with Silk Touch if needed; relocated eggs do not keep their previous cracking progress.

taming.answer: Turtle cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

identity.answer: A turtle is a passive coastal animal. Breed it with seagrass to produce eggs on its home beach. Babies shed turtle scutes when they grow up.

behavior.answer: A turtle is a passive coastal animal. Breed it with seagrass to produce eggs on its home beach. Babies shed turtle scutes when they grow up.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Breed it with seagrass to produce eggs on its home beach. Babies shed turtle scutes when they grow up.

health.answer: Its normal maximum health is 30 health points (15 hearts). Effects can change its health during play.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

health.answer: Vexes have 14 health points (7 hearts).

spawning.answer: Evokers summon vexes during combat. They do not normally spawn throughout the landscape.

drops.answer: Vexes do not drop their iron swords, even with Looting. A player or tamed-wolf kill can give experience.

combat.answer: Vexes fly through blocks and attack with swords. Walls alone will not stop them; deal with the evoker that summons them.

taming.answer: Vex cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Vex cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A vex is a small flying hostile spirit summoned by evokers. It can pass through blocks and attack with a sword, so ordinary walls are not reliable protection.

behavior.answer: A vex is a small flying hostile spirit summoned by evokers. It can pass through blocks and attack with a sword, so ordinary walls are not reliable protection.

health.answer: Villagers have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Villagers generate in villages, and can also come from breeding or curing zombie villagers. Bedrock villages occur in plains, deserts, savannas, snowy plains, taigas and snowy taigas.

drops.answer: Ordinary Bedrock villagers do not provide normal item or experience drops when killed. Obtain their goods by trading.

breeding.answer: Two adult villagers need enough food and an available bed for a baby. Each needs 3 bread or 12 carrots, potatoes or beetroots. Keep suitable beds available and allow the villagers to reach one another.

trading.answer: Adult villagers use job-site blocks to take professions and restock trades. Trading uses emeralds and goods. Babies and nitwits do not trade; trading with a villager locks its profession and existing offers.

taming.answer: Villager cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

identity.answer: A villager is a village inhabitant that can trade with players. Eligible villagers take professions from job-site blocks. Their trades depend on profession, level, and world settings.

behavior.answer: A villager is a village inhabitant that can trade with players. Eligible villagers take professions from job-site blocks. Their trades depend on profession, level, and world settings.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Eligible villagers take professions from job-site blocks. Their trades depend on profession, level, and world settings.

health.answer: Villagers have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Villagers generate in villages, and can also come from breeding or curing zombie villagers. Bedrock villages occur in plains, deserts, savannas, snowy plains, taigas and snowy taigas.

drops.answer: Ordinary Bedrock villagers do not provide normal item or experience drops when killed. Obtain their goods by trading.

breeding.answer: Two adult villagers need enough food and an available bed for a baby. Each needs 3 bread or 12 carrots, potatoes or beetroots. Keep suitable beds available and allow the villagers to reach one another.

trading.answer: Adult villagers use job-site blocks to take professions and restock trades. Trading uses emeralds and goods. Babies and nitwits do not trade; trading with a villager locks its profession and existing offers.

taming.answer: Villager v2 cannot be tamed as player-owned pets. You can still ask how to breed them.

identity.answer: A villager is a village inhabitant that can trade with players. Eligible villagers take professions from job-site blocks. Their trades depend on profession, level, and world settings.

behavior.answer: A villager is a village inhabitant that can trade with players. Eligible villagers take professions from job-site blocks. Their trades depend on profession, level, and world settings.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Eligible villagers take professions from job-site blocks. Their trades depend on profession, level, and world settings.

health.answer: Vindicators have 24 health points (12 hearts).

spawning.answer: Vindicators generate in woodland mansions and appear in raids. Mansion vindicators do not continually respawn.

drops.answer: Vindicators can drop emeralds and have separate equipment-drop chances. Bedrock raid loot has additional conditions; not every possible item drops from each kill.

combat.answer: Vindicators attack at close range with axes. Keep distance and use solid barriers rather than letting several surround you.

taming.answer: Vindicator cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Vindicator cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A vindicator is a hostile axe-wielding illager. It attacks at close range and appears in raids and certain structures.

behavior.answer: A vindicator is a hostile axe-wielding illager. It attacks at close range and appears in raids and certain structures.

health.answer: Wandering traders have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Wandering traders can appear near players in the Overworld with two trader llamas. They are temporary visitors and can despawn even if named.

drops.answer: Killing a wandering trader does not give its trading inventory. A held drinking or displayed item has separate Bedrock drop chances.

breeding.answer: Wandering traders cannot breed or become ordinary village residents.

trading.answer: Use emeralds to buy the trader’s offered goods. Its offers and stock are limited; it does not take a village profession or restock like a normal villager.

taming.answer: Wandering trader cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

identity.answer: A wandering trader is a travelling merchant that appears with trader llamas. Trade emeralds for its rotating selection of goods before it leaves.

behavior.answer: A wandering trader is a travelling merchant that appears with trader llamas. Trade emeralds for its rotating selection of goods before it leaves.

combat.answer: It does not normally attack players. Trade emeralds for its rotating selection of goods before it leaves.

health.answer: Wardens have 500 health points (250 hearts).

spawning.answer: Naturally generated sculk shriekers in the deep dark can summon a warden after repeated player warnings. A shrieker placed by a player cannot normally summon one.

drops.answer: A warden drops one sculk catalyst and a small amount of experience. Its loot is not a reward worth the danger of fighting it.

combat.answer: Wardens are blind but detect vibrations and smell nearby targets. Sneaking and wool can help manage vibrations. Their powerful melee attacks and ranged sonic boom make avoiding them safer than fighting.

taming.answer: Warden cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Warden cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: The Warden is a powerful hostile mob associated with the deep dark and sculk shriekers. It uses vibrations, smell, and a sonic attack to find and fight threats. Sneak away and avoid summoning it rather than treating it as an ordinary fight.

behavior.answer: The Warden is a powerful hostile mob associated with the deep dark and sculk shriekers. It uses vibrations, smell, and a sonic attack to find and fight threats. Sneak away and avoid summoning it rather than treating it as an ordinary fight.

spawning.answer: Wind-charge projectiles come from breezes or from using a wind charge item, depending on the projectile type.

interactions.answer: Wind charges burst on impact, pushing entities and interacting with some buttons, doors and other mechanisms. Player wind charges and breeze projectiles do not have identical rules.

identity.answer: A wind charge is a projectile that creates a gust on impact. Use wind bursts for movement tricks and activating compatible mechanisms; be careful about landing damage.

behavior.answer: A wind charge is a projectile that creates a gust on impact. Use wind bursts for movement tricks and activating compatible mechanisms; be careful about landing damage.

health.answer: Witches have 26 health points (13 hearts).

spawning.answer: Witches appear in suitable dark Overworld areas, swamp huts and raids. Lightning striking a villager can also create a witch.

drops.answer: Witches can drop redstone and items from pools including sticks, bottles, glowstone dust, gunpowder, spider eyes and sugar. A potion being drunk has a separate drop chance; these are not all guaranteed from every witch.

combat.answer: Witches throw harmful splash potions and drink potions to heal or protect themselves. Keep your distance and avoid staying inside their throwing range.

taming.answer: Witch cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Witch cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A witch is a hostile potion-using mob. It throws harmful potions and drinks useful potions to protect or heal itself.

behavior.answer: A witch is a hostile potion-using mob. It throws harmful potions and drinks useful potions to protect or heal itself.

health.answer: In Bedrock, the wither has 300 health points on Easy, 450 on Normal and 600 on Hard.

construction.answer: Build a T from four soul sand or soul soil blocks, then put three wither skeleton skulls across its top. Place the last skull last and leave the required space clear. It cannot be summoned on Peaceful.

spawning.answer: Players summon the wither using soul sand or soul soil and three wither skeleton skulls; it does not naturally wander into the world.

drops.answer: Defeating the wither drops a nether star. Bedrock also awards 50 experience, and the dropped nether star does not normally despawn.

combat.answer: The Bedrock wither fires explosive skulls and becomes more dangerous during its later phase. Prepare a secure fighting area and healing; its behavior and health differ from Java.

taming.answer: Wither cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Wither cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults. They are created using their construction or summoning method instead.

identity.answer: The Wither is a powerful summoned undead boss. It flies, fires explosive skulls, and causes destructive fights. Defeating it provides a Nether star.

behavior.answer: The Wither is a powerful summoned undead boss. It flies, fires explosive skulls, and causes destructive fights. Defeating it provides a Nether star.

health.answer: Wither skeletons have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Look in Nether fortresses at light level 7 or less. Bedrock wither fights can also produce wither skeletons during the later phase.

drops.answer: Wither skeletons can drop coal and bones. A player or tamed-wolf kill has a 2.5% skull chance; in Bedrock each Looting level adds 2 percentage points, reaching 8.5% with Looting III. A charged-creeper kill can also produce a skull. Equipment has separate chances.

combat.answer: Their melee attacks inflict Wither. Keep distance or use a barrier that takes advantage of their height.

taming.answer: Wither skeleton cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Wither skeleton cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A wither skeleton is a hostile Nether skeleton that usually fights with a sword. Its attacks inflict the Wither effect, and its rare skull drop is used to summon the Wither.

behavior.answer: A wither skeleton is a hostile Nether skeleton that usually fights with a sword. Its attacks inflict the Wither effect, and its rare skull drop is used to summon the Wither.

spawning.answer: The wither launches wither-skull projectiles during combat.

combat.answer: Wither skulls explode on impact and can apply Wither. The slower blue skull has stronger block-breaking properties than an ordinary black skull.

identity.answer: A Wither skull projectile is an explosive attack fired by the Wither. Avoid the impact and resulting harmful effects; it is not the same thing as a collectible wither skeleton skull.

behavior.answer: A Wither skull projectile is an explosive attack fired by the Wither. Avoid the impact and resulting harmful effects; it is not the same thing as a collectible wither skeleton skull.

spawning.answer: The wither launches wither-skull projectiles during combat.

combat.answer: Wither skulls explode on impact and can apply Wither. The slower blue skull has stronger block-breaking properties than an ordinary black skull.

identity.answer: A blue Wither skull is a dangerous variant of the Wither's explosive projectile. It can break blocks that resist many ordinary explosions, so do not rely on a simple wall for protection.

behavior.answer: A blue Wither skull is a dangerous variant of the Wither's explosive projectile. It can break blocks that resist many ordinary explosions, so do not rely on a simple wall for protection.

health.answer: Wild Bedrock wolves have 8 health points (4 hearts); tamed wolves have 40 health points (20 hearts).

spawning.answer: Wolf variants live in different biomes: pale in taiga; woods in forest; ashen in snowy taiga; black in old growth pine taiga; chestnut in old growth spruce taiga; rusty in sparse jungle; spotted in savanna plateau; striped in wooded badlands; snowy in grove.

variants.answer: There are nine wolf variants: pale, woods, ashen, black, chestnut, rusty, spotted, striped and snowy. Their home biomes differ. A baby inherits a parent’s variant rather than changing to match the breeding biome.

drops.answer: Wolves have no ordinary meat or fur drop. Equipped wolf armor drops separately. Experience depends on age and the kill conditions.

taming.answer: Feed bones to a wild, non-angry wolf. Each bone has a one-in-three chance to tame it. A wolf already owned by another player cannot be tamed again.

breeding.answer: Feed meat to two standing, tamed adult wolves at full health. Rotten flesh and raw chicken work. Bedrock has a one-minute breeding cooldown; do not use Java-only fish breeding rules.

interactions.answer: Tamed wolves follow their owner or can sit. Meat heals them, dyes change their collars, and wolf armor provides protection.

combat.answer: Wild wolves can become hostile when provoked, and nearby wolves may join the attack. A tamed wolf can fight for its owner. Ownership and the current anger state matter; a wolf is not always harmless.

identity.answer: A wolf is a neutral animal that can be tamed into a companion. Tame it with bones, then have it follow or sit. Tamed wolves help defend their owner and can wear wolf armor.

behavior.answer: A wolf is a neutral animal that can be tamed into a companion. Tame it with bones, then have it follow or sit. Tamed wolves help defend their owner and can wear wolf armor.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

interactions.answer: The bottle breaks on impact and releases experience orbs. It does not directly apply an enchantment to an item.

spawning.answer: Experience orbs come from activities such as suitable mob kills, mining certain ores, smelting, breeding and trading.

interactions.answer: Nearby experience orbs move toward players and are collected for experience. Mending can use collected experience to repair eligible equipment.

identity.answer: An experience orb is a small entity that players collect for experience. It contributes toward experience levels or repairs suitable equipped Mending items.

health.answer: Zoglins have 40 health points (20 hearts).

spawning.answer: A hoglin outside the Nether becomes a zoglin after about 15 seconds.

drops.answer: Zoglins can drop 1–3 rotten flesh, including babies, with applicable Looting increases.

breeding.answer: Zoglins cannot be bred.

taming.answer: Zoglins cannot be tamed.

combat.answer: Zoglins attack many nearby creatures, including players. Do not treat one as a living hoglin that can be controlled with fungi.

identity.answer: A zoglin is an undead hoglin variant created when a hoglin transforms outside the Nether. It is aggressive toward many nearby entities and cannot be bred like an ordinary hoglin.

behavior.answer: A zoglin is an undead hoglin variant created when a hoglin transforms outside the Nether. It is aggressive toward many nearby entities and cannot be bred like an ordinary hoglin.

health.answer: Bedrock zombies have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Zombies appear in suitable dark Overworld areas and from monster or trial spawners. Deserts often produce husks instead.

drops.answer: Zombies can drop 0–2 rotten flesh, with rare iron ingot, carrot or potato drops under player-kill conditions. Equipment has separate rules. A charged-creeper kill can produce a zombie head.

interactions.answer: Zombies burn in daylight unless protected. They can infect villagers: the conversion chance is 0% on Easy, 50% on Normal and 100% on Hard. A submerged zombie can become a drowned.

taming.answer: Zombie cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Zombie cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A zombie is a hostile undead mob that attacks at close range. It normally burns in direct sunlight unless protected and can transform into a drowned after suitable underwater conditions.

behavior.answer: A zombie is a hostile undead mob that attacks at close range. It normally burns in direct sunlight unless protected and can transform into a drowned after suitable underwater conditions.

combat.answer: It is a hostile mob and can attack players. It normally burns in direct sunlight unless protected and can transform into a drowned after suitable underwater conditions.

health.answer: Zombie horses have 25 health points.

spawning.answer: Zombie horsemen can appear at night or during thunderstorms in suitable plains and savanna biomes and snowy plains; Bedrock also includes ice spikes. The mounted zombie is a separate entity.

drops.answer: Zombie horses can drop 2–3 rotten flesh plus applicable equipped items. The rider has separate loot.

taming.answer: Repeatedly ride a zombie horse until it accepts you, then use suitable equipment to control it.

breeding.answer: Zombie horses cannot be bred.

combat.answer: The zombie horse itself is passive, but a mounted zombie is a separate hostile opponent. Deal with the rider without assuming the horse is making the attack.

identity.answer: A zombie horse is an undead horse variant. Its availability and riding rules depend on the game version and how it was obtained; do not assume ordinary horse breeding works.

behavior.answer: A zombie horse is an undead horse variant. Its availability and riding rules depend on the game version and how it was obtained; do not assume ordinary horse breeding works.

diet.answer: Food has different uses for breeding, taming, healing and growth.

health.answer: Zombie nautiluses have 15 health points.

spawning.answer: Some trident-wielding drowned can spawn riding zombie nautiluses outside rivers and frozen rivers. Warm-ocean spawning can produce the coral variant.

drops.answer: Zombie nautiluses can drop rotten flesh and applicable equipped items. A drowned rider has its own separate loot.

taming.answer: Feed pufferfish or a bucket of pufferfish to a zombie nautilus. Each feeding has a one-in-three taming chance.

variants.answer: Zombie nautiluses have ordinary and coral forms; the coral form is associated with warm oceans.

breeding.answer: Zombie nautilus cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

combat.answer: Untamed zombie nautiluses can retaliate with a dash and attack pufferfish; tamed ones are normally passive. A drowned rider can make the pair dangerous even though the mount and rider are separate entities.

identity.answer: A zombie nautilus is an undead aquatic nautilus variant. It can carry riders and has taming and saddling interactions under suitable conditions. Its undead behavior differs from an ordinary nautilus.

behavior.answer: A zombie nautilus is an undead aquatic nautilus variant. It can carry riders and has taming and saddling interactions under suitable conditions. Its undead behavior differs from an ordinary nautilus.

health.answer: Bedrock zombified piglins have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Zombified piglins appear in suitable Nether areas, near active Overworld Nether portals, from pigs struck by lightning, or when piglins remain outside the Nether.

drops.answer: They can drop rotten flesh and gold nuggets, with rare gold ingots under player-kill conditions. Equipped weapons have separate chances.

interactions.answer: Zombified piglins are usually neutral until provoked, then nearby members can become angry. They do not barter with gold and cannot be cured back into piglins.

taming.answer: Zombie pigman cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Zombie pigman cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A zombified piglin is a neutral undead Nether mob. Attacking one can anger nearby zombified piglins. It does not barter like an ordinary piglin.

behavior.answer: A zombified piglin is a neutral undead Nether mob. Attacking one can anger nearby zombified piglins. It does not barter like an ordinary piglin.

combat.answer: It can attack under particular conditions, so do not assume it is always harmless. Attacking one can anger nearby zombified piglins. It does not barter like an ordinary piglin.

health.answer: Bedrock zombie villagers have 20 health points (10 hearts).

spawning.answer: Zombie villagers can spawn with zombies, generate in abandoned villages and igloo basements, or result from villagers being killed by zombies. Infection depends on difficulty.

drops.answer: Zombie villagers can drop rotten flesh, rare iron ingots, carrots or potatoes, and applicable equipment under their own loot conditions.

interactions.answer: Apply Weakness, then feed a normal golden apple to start curing a zombie villager. Protect it while it converts. An enchanted golden apple is not the curing ingredient.

taming.answer: Zombie villager cannot be tamed as player-owned pets.

breeding.answer: Zombie villager cannot be bred by feeding a pair of adults.

identity.answer: A zombie villager is an undead villager variant. Apply the appropriate Weakness effect and use a golden apple to begin curing it under suitable conditions.

behavior.answer: A zombie villager is an undead villager variant. Apply the appropriate Weakness effect and use a golden apple to begin curing it under suitable conditions.

combat.answer: It is a hostile mob and can attack players. Apply the appropriate Weakness effect and use a golden apple to begin curing it under suitable conditions.

drops.answer: A broken painting can return its painting item. Removing its support makes it pop off; it is not a source of animal loot.

interactions.answer: Leave enough clear space for the painting size you want. Painting support and placement rules differ from placing a solid building block.

identity.answer: A painting is a decorative entity hung on a wall. Its size and picture depend on the available space and placement choice.

spawning.answer: Dropped items appear when players drop inventory items, blocks break, containers spill or creatures produce loot.

interactions.answer: Most dropped items despawn after five minutes while their area is ticking. Time pauses while the area is unloaded. Bedrock nether stars do not normally despawn.

drops.answer: A dropped item already represents its item stack. Pick it up rather than trying to kill it for another loot drop.

identity.answer: A dropped item is the world entity representing an item outside an inventory. Players can pick it up, and compatible nearby item stacks can merge.

drops.answer: The result depends on the falling block and its landing space. It may settle, break into an item, or be destroyed; not every falling block guarantees an item.

interactions.answer: Falling anvils and pointed dripstone can hurt entities below. Suspicious sand or gravel loses its archaeological contents when it falls and breaks, so support it before excavating.

drops.answer: The rider and spider have separate health and loot. Killing one does not automatically kill or collect the drops of the other. Ask about the spider or its specific rider for item quantities.

combat.answer: Prepare for both climbing melee attacks from the spider and ranged attacks from the rider. Removing one opponent can leave the other alive.
